questions.question:
Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.

The merchant took out the dead parrot from the cage.

options.text: The dead parrot is taken out from the cage by the merchant.
The dead parrot was taking out from the cage by the merchant.
The dead parrot was taken out from the cage by the merchant.
The dead parrot took out from the cage by the merchant.

questions.solution:
• **The correct answer is Option 3.**
 
• The structure of the given active sentence is 'Subject+V2+object+other words'.
 
• The structure of the passive sentence should be '**Object+was/were+V3+other words'.**
 
• Option 1 is wrong because the verb 'is' is used instead of 'was'.
 
• Option 2 is wrong because of the wrong usage of the verb 'taking out'.a
 
• Option 4 is wrong because the verb is in 2nd form i.e. 'took'.
 
• **The only option which satisfies the structure is 'Option 3' i.e. 'The dead parrot was taken out from the cage by the merchant.'**

questions.question:
Two different position of the same dice are shown. Which number will be at the top if 2 is at the bottom?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/fde56d655e843679c4c9ad4573d15467f22ca3764d71595c01c6de67f8e24181.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/860568bdfb3c4c18650d53bc0e3c49cff37c06259959d122ec6163a652dcbd06.png]
questions.solution:
3 is common to both the positions of the given dice.

6 and 4 are adjacent to 3 in the first position.

5 and 2 are adjacent to 3 in the second position.

Thus, the only remaining number 1 must be on the face opposite to that of 3.

This means 5, 3 and 1 are adjacent to 2.

We have 2 choices: either 6 is opposite to 2 or 4 is opposite to 2.

questions.question: When pressure is applied to a fluid, the pressure change is transmitted to every part of the fluid without any loss. Which of the following laws explains this phenomenon?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 3, i.e. __**Pascal's Law.**____**​**__

__**Concept:**__

 
 

 **Law**
 **Property/Explanation**
 
 

 Avogadro's Law
 It states that equal volumes of all gases under the same conditions of temperature and pressure contain the equal number of molecules.
 
 

 Bernoulli's Law
 
 
For a streamlined flow of an ideal liquid in a varying cross-section tube, the total energy per unit volume remains constant throughout the fluid.

 
i.e., P + (1)/(2)rho {v²} + rho gh = constant

 
 
 

 Pascal's Law
 Pascal’s Law is the principle of transmission of fluid-pressure.

 It says that "a pressure exerted anywhere in a point of the confined fluid is transmitted equally in all directions throughout the fluid”.
 
 

 Hooke's Law
 Hooke's law states that within the elastic limit the stress applied on a body is directly proportional to strain produced.
 
 

__**Explanation:**__

From the above explanation, we can see that, 

 
• **Pascal’s principle, also called Pascal’s law, in fluid (gas or liquid) mechanics, statement that in a fluid at rest in a closed container, a pressure change in one part is transmitted without loss to every portion of the fluid and to the walls of the container. **
 
• **The principle was first enunciated by the French scientist Blaise Pascal.**
 
• **The pressure is equal to the force divided by the area on which it acts. **
 
• According to Pascal’s principle, in a hydraulic system, a pressure exerted on a piston produces an equal increase in pressure on another piston in the system.
 
• If the second piston has an area 10 times that of the first, the force on the second piston is 10 times greater, though the pressure is the same as that on the first piston. This effect is exemplified by the hydraulic press, based on Pascal’s principle, which is used in such applications as hydraulic brakes.
 
• **Pascal also discovered that the pressure at a point in a fluid at rest is the same in all directions; the pressure would be the same on all planes passing through a specific point. This fact is also known as Pascal’s principle, or Pascal’s law.**
